question: Does an intervention delivered to whole groups cause the outcome?

steps.title: Define clusters
steps.text: The unit you allocate is a whole group: a school, a clinic, a village. Everyone in it gets the same arm.

quotes.text: Cluster-randomised trials (CRTs) randomise groups of individuals (“clusters”) to different interventions or sequences of interventions within a trial, as opposed to individuals.

steps.title: Say why
steps.text: Cluster when the intervention acts on the whole group, or when splitting a group would let it leak from one arm to the other.

quotes.text: CRTs are widely used in settings where interventions are delivered in an attempt to change the culture, environment or general practices and to reduce contamination between arms.
Rationale for using a cluster design.
quotes.where: item 2a, the CONSORT cluster extension's wording

steps.title: Randomise clusters
steps.text: Chance allocates the clusters, not the people. Then say how people inside each cluster came into the trial.

quotes.text: Specification that allocation was based on clusters rather than individuals and whether allocation concealment (if any) was at the cluster level, the individual participant level, or both.
quotes.where: item 9, the CONSORT cluster extension's wording

quotes.text: Mechanism by which individual participants were included in clusters for the purposes of the trial (such as complete enumeration, random sampling).
quotes.where: item 10b, the CONSORT cluster extension's wording

steps.title: Size for likeness
steps.text: People in one cluster resemble each other, so each adds less new information. The sample size must allow for it, which usually means more people.

quotes.text: The ICC is the between cluster variability divided by the total variability.

Method of calculation, number of clusters (and whether equal or unequal cluster sizes are assumed), cluster size, a coefficient of intracluster correlation (ICC or k), and an indication of its uncertainty.
quotes.where: item 7a, the CONSORT cluster extension's wording

steps.title: Analyse as clusters
steps.text: Compare the arms in a way that respects the grouping. Treating every pupil as independent makes the result look surer than it is.

quotes.text: How clustering was taken into account.
quotes.where: item 12a, the CONSORT cluster extension's wording

unit-of-analysis.text: An experimental unit is defined as the smallest entity that can be randomly assigned to a different treatment condition

limits: The card's defining paper, the CONSORT cluster extension (Campbell et al. 2012, BMJ e5661), was not read directly: it is not in Europe PMC's open full text, and bmj.com and PMC showed bot checks, which were not passed. Its item wordings are quoted as Hemming et al. (2018) reprint them.
The design effect (how much clustering inflates the sample size) is described in words only: no source's formula was read in a form that could be quoted word for word.
